newsitem.title: GERMANY: No need for independent probe of Gulf illness - Cohen.
newsitem.headline: No need for independent probe of Gulf illness - Cohen.

text.p: U.S. Defense Secretary William Cohen said on Wednesday there was no need for an independent investigation of the Pentagon's handling of Gulf War illness because the current military investigation was "very thorough".

"I think there is general disappointment in terms of he level of record-keeping that took place (during the war). Obviously it was not well handled, but I think the (current) investigation is very thorough," Cohen told reporters travelling with him on a visti to Europe.

"No," he replied when asked if the Pentagon's announcement this week that the Defense Department Inspector General would look into the issue of Gulf War chemical logs was an indication that an outside body should take over the whole investigation of Gulf War illness.

"It was an effort on our part to see to it that the public is satisfied that we are going to make a thorough investigtion, that we dig through all the facts and ...reconfirm to the American people that we are going to make a thorough investigation," Cohen added.

The Defense Department is currently investigating the causes of so-called Gulf War illness, which includes a wide range of physical complaints suffered by thousands of Gulf War veterans, but says there is no evidence of any common cause or that U.S. troops were exposed to Iraqi chemical weapons during the 1991 conflict with Iraq.
The Pentagon recently confirmed that the majority of military logs on chemical weapons information kept by U.S. military officials in Saudi Arabia during the war had been lost.
